jobs.title: Director, HR Services, Systems and Data
jobs.description:
Toronto Pearson is transforming. Now’s the time for your career to fly.
The Greater Toronto Airports Authority (GTAA) is a unique and dynamic place to work, with a bold plan to make Toronto Pearson, Canada’s leading global hub airport, a global leader in airport performance, customer care and sustainability. Together with our partners, approximately 1,900 GTAA employees are working to create a next-generation airport by innovating in all we do and striving for the most uplifting, safe and efficient experience for our passengers – all while championing the prosperity of our people, the community we call home, and our aviation partners. Join us on our journey together, as we put the joy back into travel and make Toronto Pearson the chosen place to fly and work.

What's in it for you?

•An opportunity to grow, develop, and thrive within a dynamic, and fast-growing company alongside thoughtful and passionate individuals dedicated to their work and community.
•Comprehensive benefits, including a flexible retirement program with employer matching, along with voluntary savings options (RRSP, TFSA, and Non-Registered Savings Plans).
•A flexible hybrid work environment, continuous internal and external learning opportunities, and a meaningful reward and recognition program.

What can you expect from this position?

Reporting to the Chief Human Resources Officer, the Director, HR Services, Systems & Data is a transformational leadership role accountable for modernizing and optimizing how Human Resources services are delivered across the organization. You will lead a multidisciplinary team responsible for HR Services, HR Technology, and HR Data & Analytics, driving the development of a scalable, service-oriented operating model that enhances the employee and manager experience while improving efficiency, consistency, and organizational effectiveness. As a key member of the HR leadership team, you will champion the use of technology, automation, data, and process improvement to transform HR operations, reduce administrative complexity, and enable more strategic value across the function. You will provide strategic oversight of HR systems, digital enablement, workforce analytics, governance, and service delivery, ensuring HR is equipped with the tools, insights, and capabilities required to support a high-performing and future-ready organization.

As a Director, HR Services, Systems & Data, you will:

• Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of a modern HR service
delivery model that enhances service quality, consistency, and accessibility for employees
and leaders.
• Establish and oversee centralized HR operations, including service intake, case
management, escalation processes, service standards, and performance metrics.
• Drive operational excellence through process standardization, simplification, automation,
and continuous improvement across the employee lifecycle.
• Develop and execute the HR technology strategy and roadmap, ensuring systems and
digital capabilities align with organizational priorities and employee needs.
• Provide end-to-end leadership for HR systems, including enhancements, integrations,
governance, vendor management, and ongoing optimization.
• Champion the adoption of digital tools, self-service capabilities, automation, and AIenabled
solutions to improve efficiency and user experience.
• Lead the HR data and analytics function, delivering workforce insights, dashboards,
reporting, and predictive analytics that support informed decision-making.
• Establish strong governance frameworks for HR operations, systems, and employee data,
ensuring compliance, security, privacy, and data integrity.
• Partner closely with HR leaders, IT, Payroll, Finance, and business stakeholders to deliver
integrated solutions and drive enterprise-wide HR transformation initiatives.
• Build, coach, and develop a high-performing team while fostering a culture of
accountability, innovation, customer service, and continuous learning.

This is the role for you, if you have:

• 10+ years of progressive Human Resources experience, including significant leadership
experience in HR Operations, HR Technology, HR Services, Shared Services, or HR
Transformation environments.
• A bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Information Systems,
or a related discipline; a graduate degree is considered an asset.
• A professional designation such as CHRL, CHRP, or equivalent credentials in HR,
technology, analytics, or transformation is preferred.
• Experience leading large-scale HR transformation initiatives, including operating model
redesign, service delivery optimization, and technology-enabled process improvements.
• Demonstrated success implementing, optimizing, or managing enterprise HRIS/HCM
platforms such as Dayforce, Workday, SAP, Oracle, or similar solutions.
• Experience developing and leading centralized service delivery or shared services functions
focused on service excellence and operational efficiency.
• Strong expertise in HR technology, automation, digital enablement, workforce analytics,
and data-driven decision-making.
• Proven experience building, leading, and developing high-performing teams, including
direct leadership of people leaders and cross-functional teams.
• Deep understanding of HR operations, employee lifecycle processes, service management,
data governance, and continuous improvement methodologies.
• Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to partner
effectively across executive, functional, and technical teams.
• Experience operating within large, complex, multi-stakeholder, unionized, regulated, or
customer-focused environments.
• Ability to obtain and retain Transportation Security Clearance at the designated level for the
position.

The GTAA is committed to Employment Equity and maintaining a diverse, equitable and

inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive.

Director

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Financial Performance
jobs.description:
SaskEnergy is seeking a qualified and motivated individual to join our team. Director, Enterprise Financial Performance directs and provides strategic leadership for a focused enterprise function that improves the Corporation’s financial performance through sustainable cost control, productivity improvement, revenue assurance, revenue optimization and stronger financial discipline. The Director identifies and prioritizes material opportunities, leads targeted financial and operational analysis, and works collaboratively with business and functional leaders to develop and advance practical solutions. This position leads complex and cross-functional reviews where issues require dedicated capacity, independent challenge and integrated financial and operational judgment. Business and functional leaders retain accountability for operational decisions, execution, ongoing process ownership and sustainment.

Position Details

Non-union. This position is permanent full time.

Key Accountabilities

Direct the development and management of a prioritized pipeline of material cost, productivity, revenue and financial-performance opportunities aligned with Corporate priorities and financial objectives.
Lead targeted reviews of material, recurring or cross-functional cost and performance issues to identify underlying operational, process, resource, technology and accountability drivers; quantify opportunities and recommend practical actions.
Lead or coordinate initiatives to strengthen revenue integrity and optimize revenue, including revenue leakage, billing and collection process gaps, non-tariffed service fees, cost recovery, missed billable activity and other opportunities.
Provide strategic financial analysis and independent decision support for complex or emerging matters of enterprise significance, including financial modelling, options and scenario analysis, investigations and fact finding.
Assess end-to-end accountabilities, hand-offs and operating models where financial performance issues cross organizational boundaries; facilitate decisions and support accountable leaders in implementing agreed changes.
Mobilize and coordinate the business, financial, process-improvement, technology and other expertise required to evaluate opportunities, design practical solutions and support implementation.
Work with accountable leaders to establish implementation plans, milestones, ownership and expected outcomes; identify barriers and support corrective action through to transition and sustainment.
Work with Finance and business leaders to ensure financial impacts are appropriately validated and sustainable improvements are reflected in Corporate forecasts, budgets and financial plans.
Provide concise, evidence-based recommendations, portfolio updates, risks and decisions required to the CFO, Executive and other governance bodies.
Strengthen financial acumen by helping leaders understand cost and revenue drivers and apply financial and operational information to material decisions and improvement opportunities.
Direct and develop the Enterprise Financial Performance function, establish effective operating practices and resource requirements, lead assigned employees, and oversee the effective use of matrixed and contracted resources.
Monitor relevant utility, cost-management, revenue-assurance and enterprise-performance practices and recommend approaches that can improve sustainable Corporate financial outcomes.
Other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering or a related discipline.
A professional accounting designation or other relevant professional credential is an asset. Process-improvement, project or change-management training is also beneficial.
Ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in financial management, business performance, financial analysis, operational improvement, commercial analysis, transformation or related work in a complex organization, including leadership of significant cross-functional initiatives.
Strong knowledge of regulated utility, energy or similarly asset-intensive operations and the relationship among safety, reliability, customer service, cost structures, revenues, capital investment, regulation and financial performance.
Demonstrated financial and commercial acumen, including interpretation of financial statements, cost and revenue drivers, business cases, complex financial modelling, scenario analysis and translation of operational issues into financial implications.
Demonstrated ability to identify and prioritize material opportunities, move from analysis to practical action, and influence accountable leaders without assuming operational authority.
Knowledge of revenue assurance, cost management, end-to-end process analysis, operating-model design, performance improvement, implementation and benefit-realization practices.
Exceptional judgment, facilitation, negotiation and executive communication skills, with the ability to constructively challenge established practices and work effectively across organizational boundaries.
Ability to lead and develop employees and coordinate multidisciplinary resources through ambiguity, competing priorities and sensitive organizational issues.
Must have a continuing record of professional development and continuous learning.

A suitable combination of relevant education and experience may also be considered.

Additional Information

Travel, including overnight stays away from headquarters, is required on occasion.
A Class 5 Driver’s License is required.

Application Instructions

Please apply online with your cover letter and resume outlining your qualifications.
For more information on this position, please contact Human Resources at 306-777-9091.

Closing Date

October 29, 2026

Salary Range

$135,237 - $193,956
